mutants.description: Simulates a persistent, gradually worsening mechanical drift in the radar's physical antenna position encoders due to environmental stress or wear.
mutants.failureScenario: After exposure to extreme vibration, the radar's azimuth position encoder slips by 5 degrees. The built-in test equipment fails to detect this subtle mechanical misalignment, causing all subsequent positional data to be skewed.
mutants.defenseSystemImpact: All reported target bearings are systematically incorrect. Engagement commands will direct interceptors to the wrong location, resulting in a complete failure to neutralize threats and creating a high risk of fratricide or collateral damage.

mutants.description: Simulates a significant, fixed latency spike on the data link between the sensor array and the processing unit, causing the system to operate on stale data.
mutants.failureScenario: A network switch in the data link path becomes overloaded during a high-traffic situation, introducing a consistent 3-second delay in delivering radar return packets to the tracking computer.
mutants.defenseSystemImpact: The system's view of the battlespace is dangerously outdated. A supersonic threat's actual position will be kilometers ahead of its reported track, making interception vectors incorrect and giving defenders insufficient time for evasive maneuvers.

mutants.description: Simulates an intermittent power supply brownout that temporarily degrades the radar's detection sensitivity, making it blind to stealthy or distant targets.
mutants.failureScenario: The system's power converter momentarily fails to regulate voltage under heavy processing load, causing a voltage drop that reduces the signal amplifier's gain.
mutants.defenseSystemImpact: The radar's effective range and sensitivity are drastically reduced. It will fail to detect low-RCS (stealth) targets or distant threats, creating a critical gap in the defensive perimeter and giving a false sense of security.

mutants.description: Simulates high-power electromagnetic interference (EMI) creating false 'ghost' radar returns that can saturate the tracking system.
mutants.failureScenario: The radar system is operating near a powerful communication array, whose harmonic frequencies are intermittently picked up by the receiver, creating false signal detections that pass initial filtering.
mutants.defenseSystemImpact: System resources and tracking slots are wasted on non-existent targets. This can overload the tracker, causing it to drop legitimate threats under the MAX_TRACKING_TARGETS limit, and desensitize the operator to new threat alerts.

mutants.description: Simulates a faulty configuration or software bug where the target track timeout is set to an excessively short duration, preventing stable track formation.
mutants.failureScenario: A deployed software patch contains a misconfigured constant, changing the track file timeout from 10,000 milliseconds to 1,000 due to a typo during a late-night commit.
mutants.defenseSystemImpact: The system is unable to maintain stable tracks. This prevents building historical data for flight pattern analysis and threat intent assessment. Operators are flooded with 'new track' alerts for the same objects, causing confusion and loss of situational awareness.

mutants.description: Simulates random data corruption in the raw return packets, leading to physically impossible values that could crash or mislead the threat assessment logic.
mutants.failureScenario: A faulty data cable or cosmic ray single-event upset (SEU) causes bit-flips in the digitized radar data, resulting in wildly incorrect, non-numeric, or infinite values for critical fields like Doppler shift.
mutants.defenseSystemImpact: Corrupted data can lead to NaN or Infinity values propagating through calculations. This may cause the `calculateThreatScore` to return a non-finite number, crashing the sorting algorithm in `prioritizeTargets` and triggering a complete system failsafe.

mutants.description: Simulates a persistent bias in Doppler velocity measurements due to a miscalibrated reference oscillator affected by extreme temperatures.
mutants.failureScenario: After a cold start in an arctic environment, the radar's master timing crystal has not yet reached its stable operating temperature, causing a consistent frequency offset in all Doppler measurements.
mutants.defenseSystemImpact: Threat assessment is fundamentally flawed. A high-speed inbound missile (e.g., 330 m/s) might be measured as 300 m/s, falling just under the THREAT_SPEED_THRESHOLD and being ignored until it is too late to engage effectively.
